map.summary: The document combines the LM35 temperature-sensor datasheet with Texas Instruments’ legal disclaimer. It covers the sensor’s Celsius-calibrated output, performance and electrical limits, pinouts, package variants, thermal characteristics, application circuits, and practical power, mounting, and layout guidance. It also includes ordering and compliance information, revision history, and mechanical drawings, followed by TI’s disclaimer on technical resources, developer responsibilities, applicable product terms, copyright, and document updates.
map.shortDescription: LM35 datasheet and TI disclaimer covering sensor specifications, applications, packages, ordering, and terms for using technical resources.

sections.title: LM35 Precision Temperature Sensor: Features, Applications, and Description
sections.summary: The document opens with the LM35’s features: Celsius-calibrated output with a 10 mV/°C scale, low current consumption and self-heating, wide operating range, and low output impedance. It lists applications including power supplies, battery management, HVAC, and appliances. The description explains the sensor’s linear voltage output proportional to Centigrade temperature, its factory calibration, accuracy across operating ranges, compatibility with single or split supplies, and available LM35 variants and packages.
sections.shortDescription: Introduces the LM35 temperature sensor, its key electrical and accuracy features, intended applications, and operating characteristics.

sections.title: Device Information and Sensor Circuit Examples
sections.summary: This section gives package and nominal body-size information for LM35 variants, then presents basic and full-range Centigrade sensor configurations. The full-range example specifies expected outputs at −55°C, 25°C, and 150°C and gives a resistor-selection relationship. The page also includes the datasheet’s production-data and disclaimer notice.
sections.shortDescription: Provides package dimensions and basic and full-range circuit examples for converting temperature into output voltage.

sections.title: Contents and Datasheet Section Guide
sections.summary: The table of contents outlines the datasheet, from revision history and pin functions through electrical specifications, typical characteristics, detailed device description, application implementation, power recommendations, layout, documentation support, and mechanical and orderable information. It identifies subsections and page numbers to help readers navigate the technical material.
sections.shortDescription: Maps the LM35 datasheet’s sections, including specifications, application guidance, support resources, and package information.

sections.title: Revision History
sections.summary: The revision-history pages list updates from revisions C through H. Changes include corrections to the TO-CAN pinout view, added pin numbers, an equation-unit correction, an updated recommended supply-voltage range, and the addition of datasheet sections covering pin functions, ESD, device operation, applications, layout, support, and ordering information. A units correction from W to Ω is also noted.
sections.shortDescription: Summarizes changes made across successive revisions of the LM35 datasheet.

sections.title: Pin Configuration and Functions
sections.summary: This section presents pin configurations for the TO-92, TO-220, TO-CAN, and 8-pin SOIC packages, with package-specific orientation and connection notes. It identifies VOUT, GND, and +VS, marks unused pins as no connection, and notes that package tabs or cases may connect to ground. A warning distinguishes the LM35DT pinout from the discontinued LM35DP. The pin-function table describes the analog temperature output, ground, supply, and unconnected pins.
sections.shortDescription: Shows package pinouts and explains the LM35’s output, ground, supply, and no-connect pins.

sections.title: Specifications: Maximum Ratings, ESD, Operating Conditions, and Thermal Data
sections.summary: The specifications section reports supply-voltage, output-voltage, output-current, junction-temperature, and storage-temperature limits, with cautions that exceeding absolute maximum ratings may damage the device. It gives the human-body-model ESD rating and cites JEDEC guidance. Recommended conditions specify temperature ranges by LM35 variant and a 4 V to 30 V supply. Thermal information compares package thermal resistance values and references application reports for additional guidance.
sections.shortDescription: Lists absolute maximum limits, ESD robustness, recommended operating ranges, and package thermal metrics.

sections.title: Electrical Characteristics: LM35A and LM35CA Limits
sections.summary: The LM35A and LM35CA electrical-characteristics section specifies test conditions and limits for accuracy, nonlinearity, sensor gain, load and line regulation, and supply current. It also details quiescent current across supply voltages and temperatures, its temperature coefficient, minimum temperature for rate accuracy, and long-term stability. Notes explain limit categories and measurement methods.
sections.shortDescription: Summarizes LM35A and LM35CA electrical limits, including accuracy, regulation, supply and quiescent current, temperature-related specifications, and test notes.

sections.title: LM35A and LM35CA Electrical Characteristics
sections.summary: Section 6.6 lists electrical characteristics for the LM35A and LM35CA. It specifies operating-temperature ranges and test setup, then provides accuracy limits at several ambient temperatures, nonlinearity, average sensor gain, load regulation, and line regulation. Notes explain how accuracy and nonlinearity are defined, distinguish production-tested limits from design limits, and describe regulation testing.
sections.shortDescription: Presents LM35A and LM35CA accuracy, nonlinearity, sensor gain, load and line regulation specifications, plus applicable temperature conditions and measurement definitions.

sections.title: LM35A and LM35CA Electrical Characteristics (Continued)
sections.summary: This continuation completes the LM35A and LM35CA specifications. It gives typical and maximum quiescent-current values at 5 V and 30 V across stated temperature conditions, change in quiescent current, temperature coefficient, minimum temperature for rate accuracy, and long-term stability. It also reiterates the operating conditions and defines quiescent current by reference to Figure 14.
sections.shortDescription: Continues the LM35A and LM35CA characteristic tables with quiescent-current limits, current variation, temperature coefficient, rate-accuracy temperature, and stability.

sections.title: LM35, LM35C, and LM35D Electrical Characteristics: Limits
sections.summary: Section 6.7 sets out electrical-characteristic limits for the LM35, LM35C, and LM35D under specified temperature and supply conditions. The table covers accuracy by device and temperature, nonlinearity, sensor gain, load and line regulation, quiescent current at multiple supply conditions, change and temperature coefficient of quiescent current, rate-accuracy temperature, and long-term stability. Notes define tested and design limits and the measurement conventions.
sections.shortDescription: Summarizes limits for LM35, LM35C, and LM35D, including accuracy, nonlinearity, gain, regulation, current consumption, and stability.

sections.title: LM35, LM35C, and LM35D Electrical Characteristics
sections.summary: Section 6.8 restates the applicable operating-temperature ranges and standard test setup, then begins the electrical-characteristics table for LM35 and LM35C/LM35D. The visible entries cover accuracy at specified temperatures, nonlinearity across the rated range, and sensor gain as an average slope, including tested- and design-limit rows.
sections.shortDescription: Introduces the detailed characteristic table for LM35, LM35C, and LM35D and begins its accuracy, nonlinearity, and sensor-gain entries.

sections.title: Overview of LM35 sensor operation, performance, and practical application considerations.
sections.summary: LM35-series sensors provide a precision analog output proportional to Celsius temperature, with a transfer function of 10 mV/°C. They require no external calibration, have low output impedance and low self-heating, and operate over model-specific temperature ranges. The section also describes their output-stage limitations, typical characteristics, and application guidance, including precautions for capacitive loads and electrically noisy wiring.
sections.shortDescription: Overview of LM35 sensor operation, performance, and practical application considerations.

sections.title: LM35 Specifications and Temperature-Sensor Application Examples
sections.summary: Lists the LM35’s accuracy at 25°C and across its full temperature range, along with its 10 mV/°C temperature slope. Introduces the typical-application section and presents system-example schematics, including two-wire remote temperature sensors, a grounded sensor, a single-supply thermometer, and a 4-to-20 mA current source.
sections.shortDescription: Covers LM35 accuracy and temperature slope specifications, then illustrates basic sensor circuits for remote sensing, single-supply use, and current-source output.

sections.title: LM35 System Examples: Thermometers, Converters, and Displays
sections.summary: Continues the LM35 system examples with Fahrenheit and Centigrade thermometer circuits, including analog-meter and expanded-scale designs. Shows serial and parallel temperature-to-digital converters, a dot-mode bar-graph display with resistor-trimming guidance, and a voltage-to-frequency converter with isolated output.
sections.shortDescription: Presents example circuits that turn LM35 temperature readings into Fahrenheit or Centigrade measurements, digital output, bar graphs, and frequency signals.

sections.title: Power Supply Recommendations and Thermal Layout Guidance
sections.summary: Recommends bypassing the LM35 supply with 0.1 μF in noisy environments, with larger capacitance as needed. Layout guidance covers coupling the sensor thermally to a surface, limiting ambient-air effects through lead wiring and epoxy, mounting and protecting packages against moisture and corrosion, and using heat fins or added thermal mass. A table compares thermal resistance for package types and operating environments, with notes on the test setups.
sections.shortDescription: Explains LM35 supply bypassing, sensor mounting and insulation practices, and thermal resistance values under different conditions.

sections.title: LM35 Layout Example
sections.summary: Provides a layout example identifying vias to the ground and power planes, the LM35 pin arrangement, and a 0.01 μF capacitor.
sections.shortDescription: Shows a board-layout example with supply and ground connections and a local bypass capacitor.

sections.title: Device and Documentation Support
sections.summary: Explains how to register for datasheet update notifications and lists TI community and design-support resources. Includes trademark information, an electrostatic-discharge handling caution, a glossary reference, and an introduction to mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.
sections.shortDescription: Directs readers to documentation updates and TI community resources, and summarizes trademark, ESD, glossary, and packaging-information notices.

sections.title: Package Option Addendum
sections.summary: Introduces the package option addendum and its packaging-information table. The visible headings include orderable part number, status, material type, package and pin count, quantity and carrier, RoHS and finish details, moisture sensitivity, operating-temperature range, and part marking.
sections.shortDescription: Begins the packaging information table for orderable part numbers, package characteristics, compliance, and operating temperature.

sections.title: LM35 Orderable Parts: First Listing
sections.summary: The listing covers active, production LM35 variants in TO and TO-92 packages. LM35AH options are rated −55 to 150°C; CAH and CH options are −40 to 110°C. CAZ and CZ TO-92 variants include large tape-and-reel or bulk ordering options, with listed temperature ranges of either −55 to 150°C or −40 to 110°C. The rows also distinguish RoHS status, carrier, lead-finish/MSL information, and package-specific part markings.
sections.shortDescription: Lists LM35AH, CAH, CAZ, CH, and CZ orderable variants with package, quantity, shipping, compliance, temperature range, and part-marking details.

sections.title: LM35 Orderable Parts: Repeated Listing
sections.summary: This table repeats the LM35 orderable options: LM35AH variants in TO packages; CAH and CH variants in TO packages; and CAZ and CZ variants in TO-92 packages. All entries are marked active and in production. Package quantities and carriers vary, including 500-piece options, 2000-piece large tape and reel, and 1800-piece bulk. RoHS status, lead-finish/MSL information, temperature ranges, and part markings are provided for each option.
sections.shortDescription: Repeats the LM35 orderable-parts table, detailing active variants and their package, fulfillment, compliance, and operating-temperature attributes.

sections.title: LM35 Orderable Parts: Third Listing
sections.summary: The table again identifies LM35 orderable variants as active production parts. It includes AH, CAH, and CH devices in TO packages and CAZ and CZ devices in TO-92 packages. The listed options differ in package quantity, shipping carrier, RoHS status, lead-finish/MSL rating, operating-temperature range, and part marking. AH versions cover −55 to 150°C, while CAH and CH versions cover −40 to 110°C; TO-92 CAZ and CZ listings show both temperature ranges depending on suffix.
sections.shortDescription: Presents another repeated LM35 orderable-parts table with ordering and environmental details for AH, CAH, CAZ, CH, and CZ variants.

sections.title: Orderable Parts Table Header
sections.summary: A new orderable-parts table begins with columns for part number, status, material type, package, pin count, package quantity, carrier, ball material, peak reflow, RoHS, lead finish, MSL rating, operating temperature, and part marking. Footnote markers are shown, but no part entries appear in this section.
sections.shortDescription: Begins the next LM35 orderable-parts table and displays its column headings and explanatory footnote markers.

sections.title: LM35AH, CAH, CAZ, CH, and CZ Orderable Parts
sections.summary: The table records active production LM35AH, LM35CAH, LM35CAZ, LM35CH, and LM35CZ options. Packages are TO (NDV) or TO-92 (LP), with three pins. TO-92 versions are supplied in large tape-and-reel or bulk, while TO (NDV) variants use small tape-and-reel or other carriers. RoHS status and temperature range vary by suffix: AH options cover −55 to 150°C; CAH, CH, and NOPB CAZ/CZ options cover −40 to 110°C; non-NOPB CAZ/CZ options cover −55 to 150°C. Markings are LM35AH, LM35CAH, LM35CH, or LM35 followed by CAZ/CZ. The entries include both base and .B part numbers.
sections.shortDescription: Lists package, status, quantity, carrier, RoHS, lead-finish, moisture-sensitivity, operating-temperature, and marking details for LM35AH, CAH, CAZ, CH, and CZ orderable variants.

sections.title: Repeated LM35 Orderable-Part Table
sections.summary: This table repeats the active production entries for LM35AH, LM35CAH, LM35CAZ, LM35CH, and LM35CZ variants, including .B and NOPB options. It specifies three-pin TO (NDV) or TO-92 (LP) packages, packaging quantities and carriers, RoHS status, lead finish, MSL rating, operating-temperature ranges, and part markings. AH variants are rated −55 to 150°C; other listed temperature ranges depend on package and suffix, including −40 to 110°C. TO-92 options use large tape-and-reel or bulk packaging; TO (NDV) options use small tape-and-reel or other packaging.
sections.shortDescription: Repeats the LM35AH, CAH, CAZ, CH, and CZ orderable-part entries with their package and shipping specifications.

sections.title: LM35DH, DMX, DT, DZ, and H Package Options
sections.summary: The section lists LM35 orderable package variants, including LM35DH, LM35DMX, LM35DT, LM35DZ, and LM35H. Entries detail lifecycle status, package and pin count, shipping carrier and quantity, RoHS and lead-finish information, moisture-sensitivity level, operating-temperature range, and part marking. Most variants are active; the non-NOPB LM35DMX and LM35DT options are NRND. LM35DZ options include tape-and-reel, ammo, and bulk packaging with different temperature ranges. Repeated table content presents the same ordering details.
sections.shortDescription: Lists LM35 orderable variants and their lifecycle status, package, shipping, compliance, operating-temperature, and marking details.

sections.title: LM35 ordering, compliance, temperature-range, and package-material details.
sections.summary: The material lists LM35 temperature-sensor orderable variants and their status, package, pin count, order quantity, shipping carrier, RoHS compliance, lead finish, moisture-sensitivity rating, operating-temperature range, and part marking. It also explains TI’s status and material-type terms and related RoHS, lead-finish, MSL, and marking notes. Packaging details cover tape-and-reel and box dimensions for LM35DMX/NOPB, tube dimensions for LM35DT variants, and package outline and board-layout information for the TO-can and SOIC packages.
sections.shortDescription: LM35 ordering, compliance, temperature-range, and package-material details.

sections.title: SOIC Package Dimensions and Assembly Guidance
sections.summary: This section completes the SOIC package mechanical drawing, including dimensional tolerances, drawing notes, board land-pattern examples, solder-mask details, and stencil design guidance. It references applicable JEDEC and IPC standards and notes that fabrication and assembly recommendations can vary by site.
sections.shortDescription: SOIC package dimensions, board layout, and stencil recommendations.

sections.title: TO-92 Package Outline, Board Layout, and Tape Specifications
sections.summary: This section describes the TO-92 package outline and its straight- and formed-lead options, with key dimensions, drawing notes, and shipping-method availability. It also provides example board layouts for both lead options and tape specifications for the formed-lead package.
sections.shortDescription: TO-92 package dimensions, land patterns, and tape specifications.

sections.title: TO-220 Package Outline and Board Layout
sections.summary: This section gives the TO-220 transistor-outline dimensions, pin identification, and package drawing notes, followed by an example board land pattern and solder-mask opening. The drawing identifies controlling dimensions and references the JEDEC TO-220 registration.
sections.shortDescription: TO-220 package dimensions and example board layout.

sections.title: Important Notice, Disclaimer, and Copyright
sections.summary: This section states Texas Instruments’ disclaimer for technical data and design resources, outlines developer responsibilities and limits on resource use, and notes the applicable product terms. It concludes with the copyright and document update date.
sections.shortDescription: TI resource disclaimer, usage terms, and copyright notice.
